title: Graph transformations
examples: When I see f(x+3), does that mean I move right or left?
Is the stretch factor 'a' always positive?
Does the order of transformations matter?

explain.say: Today we look at how to change graphs. We start with a basic function, say y equals x squared. This is our starting point for all our changes.
If we add a number outside the function, like plus three, we move the graph up. This is a vertical shift up by three units. So we look at f(x) plus three.

items: Start with y = f(x) (the basic function)
Add a number outside: y = f(x) + 3 (moves graph up)
Add a number inside: y = f(x + 2) (moves graph left)

explain.say: If we add a number inside the function, like x plus two, we move the graph left. This is a horizontal shift left by two units. So we look at f(x plus 2).
Multiplying the whole function by a number, say two, stretches the graph vertically. This makes the graph twice as tall. This is written as two times f(x).
If we multiply the x by a number, say two, we compress the graph horizontally. This makes the graph half as wide. This is written as f(two x).

faq.q: If I see f(x) minus a number, like f(x minus 4), does that mean I move right or left?
faq.a: It means you move the graph to the right. Remember that inside changes are opposites of what you expect. You are changing x to x minus four.
asks: How do I shift right using the function notation?

faq.q: When I see a negative sign outside, like minus f(x), what does that do to the graph?
faq.a: It reflects the graph across the x axis. Every y value becomes its opposite, so the graph flips upside down.
asks: What is the effect of multiplying by negative one?
How do I flip a graph vertically?

faq.q: Does the order of shifting and stretching matter?
faq.a: Yes, the order matters a lot. You must apply the shifts and stretches in a specific order to get the correct final graph.
asks: Can I stretch then shift, or shift then stretch?
Is there a rule for the order of operations?

faq.q: What is the difference between f(x) plus a number and a times f(x)?
faq.a: The first moves the graph up or down, which is vertical. The second stretches the graph up or down, which is also vertical.
asks: What is the difference between adding and multiplying outside?
Which one affects the y-value directly?

faq.q: If I see f(x) divided by two, is that the same as f(x) times one half?
faq.a: Yes, they are mathematically the same thing. Dividing by two is the same as multiplying by one divided by two.
asks: Can I write f(x)/2 as f(x)0.5?
Is division the same as multiplying by the reciprocal?

facts: Adding a constant outside the function shifts the graph vertically.
Adding a constant inside the function shifts the graph horizontally.
Multiplying the entire function by a constant stretches or compresses it vertically.
Multiplying the independent variable x by a constant stretches or compresses it horizontally.

quiz.say: What is the transformation shown by y equals f(x) plus five?

options.show: Horizontal shift right by five units.
options.say: Horizontal shift right by five units.

options.show: Vertical stretch by a factor of five.
options.say: Vertical stretch by a factor of five.

options.show: Vertical shift up by five units.
options.say: Vertical shift up by five units.

quiz.why: Adding a constant outside the function always causes a vertical shift up.

wrong.0: This confuses the outside addition with an inside change.
wrong.2: This confuses vertical shifts with horizontal reflections.

quiz.say: If the graph of y equals x squared is transformed to y equals f(x minus three), what is the shift?

options.show: A shift of three units to the right.
options.say: A shift of three units to the right.

options.show: A shift of three units to the left.
options.say: A shift of three units to the left.

options.show: A vertical shift down by three units.
options.say: A vertical shift down by three units.

options.show: A stretch by a factor of three.
options.say: A stretch by a factor of three.

quiz.why: Inside changes are always opposite to the direction stated, so x minus three means moving right.

wrong.1: This incorrectly assumes that subtracting means moving left.
wrong.2: This confuses the horizontal input change with a vertical output change.
wrong.3: This confuses the constant inside with a vertical stretch factor.

quiz.say: Which transformation results in the graph being flipped over the x axis?

options.show: Vertical shift down by one unit.
options.say: Vertical shift down by one unit.

options.show: Horizontal compression by a factor of two.
options.say: Horizontal compression by a factor of two.

quiz.why: A negative sign multiplying the whole function flips every y value to its opposite.

wrong.0: This would be represented by f(-x), not -f(x).
wrong.1: This confuses reflection with a simple vertical translation.
wrong.2: This confuses the negative sign with a horizontal scaling factor.
